func createNewHeader(prevHeader *types.Header, l1info *L1Info, baseFee *big.Int, _chainConfig *params.ChainConfig) *types.Header {
	var lastBlockHash common.Hash
	blockNumber := big.NewInt(0)
	timestamp := uint64(0)
	coinbase := common.Address{}
	if l1info != nil {
		timestamp = l1info.l1Timestamp
		coinbase = l1info.poster
	}
	extra := common.Hash{}.Bytes()
	mixDigest := common.Hash{}
	if prevHeader != nil {
		lastBlockHash = prevHeader.Hash()
		blockNumber.Add(prevHeader.Number, big.NewInt(1))
		if timestamp < prevHeader.Time {
			timestamp = prevHeader.Time
		}
		copy(extra, prevHeader.Extra)
		mixDigest = prevHeader.MixDigest
	}
	header := &types.Header{
		ParentHash:  lastBlockHash,
		UncleHash:   types.EmptyUncleHash, // Post-merge Ethereum will require this to be types.EmptyUncleHash
		Coinbase:    coinbase,
		Root:        [32]byte{},    // Filled in later
		TxHash:      [32]byte{},    // Filled in later
		ReceiptHash: [32]byte{},    // Filled in later
		Bloom:       [256]byte{},   // Filled in later
		Difficulty:  big.NewInt(1), // Eventually, Ethereum plans to require this to be zero
		Number:      blockNumber,
		GasLimit:    l2pricing.GethBlockGasLimit,
		GasUsed:     0,
		Time:        timestamp,
		Extra:       extra,     // used by NewEVMBlockContext
		MixDigest:   mixDigest, // used by NewEVMBlockContext
		Nonce:       [8]byte{}, // Filled in later; post-merge Ethereum will require this to be zero
		BaseFee:     baseFee,
	}

locations: How the node derives safe and finalized
observations: Safe/finalized heads are derived from batch posting and parent-chain confirmation tags, subject to node configuration.
Parent-chain reorgs roll back child state and transactions after the common ancestor.
RPC finality is not an application-callable certificate.
Sequencer execution, Ethereum batch posting, and Ethereum finality are separate stages.
Documentation reports a seven-day canonical withdrawal challenge period, separate from transaction finality; no deployment-parameter audit was performed.
Protocol governance and permissioned BoLD validators remain chain trust assumptions.
These are primary documentation observations, not independently verified L1 governance storage.
